newsitem.title: POLAND: PBR eyes foreign partner to take 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: PBR eyes foreign partner to take 25 pct.

text.p: Polski Bank Rozwoju SA (PBR), a mid-sized Polish bank, wants to find a foreign investor which would take at least a 25 percent stake in PBR, its president said on Wednesday.

Mieczyslaw Groszek said however, that no decisions would be made before the public offer of Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK), expected at the turn of the third quarter, as PBR was in a consortium looking to take over the larger PBK.

"Within a short period of time we want to have a foreign institutional investor, such as an investment bank, in PBR...but (the time frame) will depend on how the PBK issue turns out," Groszek told a news conference.
"We are ready for the foreign investor to take a significant stake (of PBR) at 25 to 33 percent," Groszek said.
Groszek said PBR was looking for the foreign investor to give know-how in international financial market activites as well as infrastruture projects and in servicing large firms.
PBR is in a consortium with insurer Warta SA, Bank Przemyslowo Handlowy SA and Kredyt Bank SA to take over the state-owned PBK.
